newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt paper to be priced at market level.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt paper to be priced at market level.

text.p: Russian government paper will be priced in line with the current yield trend at Wednesday's auctions, as the Finance Ministry needs little money for repayment and the market has fallen into a summer lull, dealers said on Tuesday.
ON WEDNESDAY
The Finance Ministry sells:
*4.00 trln rbls of 182-day T-bills (series 21081)
*6.00 trln rbls of 364-day T-bills (series 21082)
The Finance Ministry repays:
*6.72 trln rbls of 259-day T-bill (series 22058)
ON TUESDAY
*Average yield fell to 17.9 pct from 18.1 pct on Monday
*Turnover rose to 3.55 trln rbls from 2.75 trln rbls
*Central bank sold 329 bln rbls of T-bills
*Banks transferred 2.39 trln rbls for trading
Dealers forecast the average yield on the series 21081 GKO discount Treasury bills would be in the 16.51-17.80 percent range.
The series 22077 bills, maturing on January 14, 1998, the closest maturity date to the new issue, on Tuesday closed at 92.92, to yield 16.31 percent.
Dealers forecast the average yield for the series 21082 T-bills would be in the 18.72-18.93 percent range.
The series 21080 bills, maturing on July 22, 1998, the closest maturity date to the new issue, on Tuesday closed at 84.45, to yield 18.77 percent.

"There is a summer calm on the market," said Natsionalny Rezervny Bank trader Konstantin Demchenko. "T-bill trend stability and the small repayment volume allow us to suggest there will be enough money for repayment and the one-year paper will yield 18.8 percent."
Russian government paper yields have been slipping steadily for the last few months, and the authorities have made it clear they will encourage a further decline.
Dealers said foreign investors, usually the market's engine, have already bought enough one-year paper, and there were no other factor which could move prices.
"I think a wave of foreign investment will come in the autumn, if Russia's credit rating is revised," said Raiffeisen Bank dealer Alexander Losev.
"Besides, last week's fall in forward deals, which pushed down the yields of long-term paper, makes investment now less attractive."
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
